deeper_dives.thesis: Autonomous agents went from demo-ware to daily drivers in 2026. But the gap between 'impressive demo' and 'reliable tool' is massive. 1. Start narrow: one task, one tool, one feedback loop
2. Build in guardrails before capability (kill switches, budget limits, scope constraints)
3. Test adversarially: what happens when the agent encounters edge cases?
4. Add persistence: agents need memory to avoid repeating mistakes
5. Monitor: log everything, review regularly, prune bad patterns
6. Scale horizontally: multiple narrow agents > one general agent

deeper_dives.title: Red-Team Your Own Agent — prompt-injection CI from the jailbreak corpus
deeper_dives.thesis: The catalog holds both halves of a loop nobody has closed. On one side sit offense corpora and autonomous attackers — L1B3RT4S still landing on GPT-5, an agent that goes from one sentence to a verified exploit, scanners hunting exposed AI servers. On the other sit the pipes that pour untrusted text into your agent — Agent Reach reading Reddit and X, 90k-skill hubs, one-command skill installers. Point the attacker inward and you get prompt-injection CI — every skill install and harness change gets replayed against a jailbreak-and-hijack suite before it touches your keys.
deeper_dives.why_it_matters: Solo builders now run agents with real API keys, inboxes and broker access, and Noma's research shows most automations hand data to anyone who simply asks. Whoever ships a cheap, repeatable injection test owns the trust layer for every one-person agent shop — and sleeps through their own cron jobs.
action_sketch: Build a 50-case suite this week — 20 L1B3RT4S-style jailbreaks, 20 Noma-style 'just ask for the data' hijacks planted in fake Reddit/X posts fetched via Agent Reach, 10 sponsored-option nudges — and run it against your harness with a canary secret in the environment

Wire it as a pre-install hook: any new skill from find-skills or a skills hub gets diffed, then the suite reruns with that skill loaded; fail the install if the canary leaks or a tool call goes outside the allowlist
Add the sandboxing layer from the portfolio-projects post — per-skill capability manifests (network, filesystem, secrets) — and measure how many suite cases each manifest blocks
Falsifier: if a plain allowlist on outbound tool calls blocks ≥95% of the suite with no skill-level testing, the CI layer is overkill and a static policy file is the whole answer
prerequisites: An agent harness with hooks (Claude Code or similar)
A throwaway canary secret and a disposable test account
Test only harnesses, accounts and keys you own

deeper_dives.title: Skills That Earn Their Lines — benchmark-gated self-editing plus subtraction
deeper_dives.thesis: Successor to the harness and second-brain dives. Those stop at 'append a lesson after every mistake'. The catalog now holds the missing machinery — Microsoft SkillOpt rewrites skills only when a benchmark improves, bilevel autoresearch adds a coach loop over the worker, Prime Agent rewrites its own harness to 95.5% on ARC-AGI-3 — and, crucially, evidence that subtraction matters as much as addition: Boris Cherny's simple mode and the setup-purge post show stale rules make newer models dumber. Combine them into a ratchet that both adds and deletes rules, keeping only edits that beat a held-out eval.
deeper_dives.why_it_matters: Every power user's CLAUDE.md grows monotonically until it is a tax on every call. A two-way, eval-gated ratchet turns rule accretion into measured improvement, and the winning traces become fine-tuning data you can push into a small local model with Soup.
action_sketch: Export your last 3 months of Claude history, have a small model tag 40 representative tasks with pass/fail criteria — that is your held-out eval
Run an ablation sweep: drop each CLAUDE.md rule and skill one at a time, rerun the eval, delete anything whose removal does not hurt the score
Add the SkillOpt loop on a nightly cron — skills log issues, an optimizer proposes edits, only score-improving edits merge; export passing traces for a Soup fine-tune later
Falsifier: if eval scores vary more between two identical runs than between best and worst rule sets, your eval is too noisy and the whole ratchet is optimizing noise
prerequisites: A CLAUDE.md and skills folder with some history
A cheap model for grading (Haiku-class or local)

Week 3: plot the series on an A3 pen plotter (AxiDraw-class or a DIY drawing machine) with two pen weights, photograph per the print-on-demand guide, list originals plus POD reproductions, and submit to one grant
Falsifier: if scanned or ripped meshes produce unreadable line mush unless you hand-pick every path, or if plotted originals cannot sell above the POD print price, the loop is a toy, not a practice

deeper_dives.title: Strategy Autoresearch — the judge is the product, not the agent
deeper_dives.thesis: Self-rewriting loops (Karpathy-style autoresearch, bilevel coach loops, Microsoft SkillOpt) keep any edit that beats a benchmark. Point one at trading and it becomes an industrial overfitting machine — the backtest is the benchmark, and the loop will beat it ten thousand times. The quant saves already hold the fix: probability of backtest overfitting, permutation tests, transaction costs and backtest-to-live drift. Wire those in as the loop's judge, and use the loop's own log as the exact count of trials — the number human quants never know.
deeper_dives.why_it_matters: A solo builder can run more strategy variants in a weekend than a small fund tests in a quarter. The difference between that being an edge and a casino is whether the gate deflates for every attempt. Most likely you learn you have no edge, cheaply, and that's worth money too.
action_sketch: Wrap a vectorized backtester (VectorBT) in a SkillOpt-style loop where Claude proposes strategy edits and every proposal is appended to a trials table with its parameters and result.

Replace 'beats benchmark' with a judge that needs all four: positive after realistic fees, beats 95% of a permutation null, deflated Sharpe positive using the trials-table count, and a held-out year scored once at the end.
Have a second model (Codex or GPT) audit each surviving strategy's code for look-ahead bias before it reaches paper trading; monitor live drift with Wasserstein distance and auto-retire on breach.
falsifier: seed the loop with pure-noise synthetic prices. If anything passes the judge, the judge is broken — fix it before you show it a real market.
prerequisites: Python and VectorBT or similar backtester
Clean historical data with realistic cost assumptions
Discipline to treat 'no survivors' as a valid result

deeper_dives.why_it_matters: For people with ADHD or executive-function friction, the failure is rarely missing information. The information is hidden in a terminal or app they have to remember to open. A glanceable surface with one-tap input removes the remembering step, which is the step that fails.

Run 14 days logging glance-triggered actions (taps within 2 min of a display change) and agent wait time before/after.

Add the promotion rule: 20 consecutive passes moves a class one tier down, any fail moves it back up; track dollars saved per class

'Build yourself a CLI for this program' covers apps with no API, Reverse Engineer Anything and the Ghidra-backed REA MCP explain closed binaries, and Claude Code already strips a smart TV over WiFi. Put these together and any legacy or closed tool becomes agent-drivable — and Bending Spoons' acquire-and-rebuild playbook shows what that is worth when the software is stagnant.
deeper_dives.why_it_matters: The long tail of MCP-less software — dental scheduling suites, MLS portals, ancient ERPs — is where small businesses lose hours. Whoever can wrap one in a reliable agent-built CLI sells the finished work rather than the software, which is exactly the AI-native-service model YC is asking for.

For the stubborn actions, run Reverse Engineer Anything (or REA MCP for native binaries) to find the underlying file formats or local endpoints, and replace UI clicks with direct calls
Wrap the CLI as an MCP server, run a week of real tasks through it, and price the result as a monthly 'we run it for you' service
Falsifier: if the wrapper breaks on more than one vendor update per month, the maintenance cost eats the margin and this is a consulting gig, not an arbitrage
prerequisites: Comfort with reverse-engineering legality in your jurisdiction
Access to the target software you are licensed to use

A phone can now capture that room as a Gaussian splat, and Gausseous makes the splat react to audio in a browser. Record the room's acoustics in the same session and the sound and the image come from one capture of one place.
deeper_dives.why_it_matters: A two-person act with a phone gets a music video format where the place itself moves with the tune — no crew, no generated faces, and the result is documentary, not synthetic. It also gives folk and field-recording traditions a native visual form instead of borrowing pop-video tropes.
action_sketch: Scan one meaningful room (a porch, a church, a barn) with a phone splat app (Polycam or Luma), then load the .ply into Gausseous and drive it with a rough recording of one tune
In the same session, record a clap or sine-sweep impulse response of the room and convolve your dry instrument recording with it, so the audio carries that room's acoustics
Cut a 60-second vertical piece — real performance footage intercut with the reacting splat — and A/B it against a plain performance video on the same account
Falsifier: if low-light interior scans come out too noisy to read, or the splat cut loses watch-through to the plain performance video, the format is a gimmick

deeper_dives.thesis: A student cleared $100K+ on Polymarket weather contracts with a dorm-built weather station, and a separate trader harvests contracts already sitting at 99c. Put those next to free real-time feeds (NASA EONET, SDR-received weather satellite images, public EIA/HIFLD infrastructure data, live plane and ship layers) and the pattern is clear — the edge on event contracts is not a smarter model, it is a faster or closer read of the exact source the contract settles on. A student cleared $100K+ on Polymarket weather contracts with a dorm-built weather station.

Paper-trade only the final six hours before resolution, with a scheduled agent comparing your live reading to the market's implied probability and to the 99c harvest opportunities in the same window.

deeper_dives.thesis: Open candlestick foundation models like Kronos give you a forecast on every bar, and a hedge-fund stress test says it fails on many levels. A separate save shows the better question: a small logistic regression that predicts tomorrow's efficiency ratio (trend versus chop) and skips the choppy days lifted almost every metric over two years out of sample. Physics-flavored measures in the quant collection — Lempel-Ziv compressibility, Hurst exponent, Lyapunov exponent, hidden Markov regimes — are all measures of the same thing: is this market forecastable right now? Use them as a confidence gate on the foundation model, not as signals.
deeper_dives.why_it_matters: You stop asking a model to be right everywhere and only ask it to be right where structure exists. That turns a free open model plus a few cheap statistics into something you can actually size positions with.
action_sketch: Run Kronos zero-shot on two years of hourly BTC and QQQ and log every forecast with its realized error.
Compute rolling efficiency ratio, Lempel-Ziv complexity and Hurst for each bar, bucket bars into tradeability quintiles, and plot Kronos error per quintile.
If error falls across quintiles, fit the efficiency-ratio-style logistic model to predict next-period tradeability and paper-trade Kronos only in the top bucket.
falsifier: if Kronos error is flat across tradeability quintiles, the complexity measures say nothing about this model's skill and the gate is decoration.
prerequisites: Python, Hugging Face access to the Kronos weights

Falsifier: if agent CAD needs more print iterations than your own hand CAD on 3 of 3 objects, the scan-to-parametric step isn't ready — the fitting step, not the scanner, is the bottleneck.

deeper_dives.title: Mission Control for 80 Agents — Conway's law meets game UI
deeper_dives.thesis: Once you run more than a handful of agents, the bottleneck is your attention, not tokens. Casey Muratori's point that Conway's law now applies to agents says the interface and the agent org chart are the same design problem. Feed a Booking.com-style trace bus into a game-engine front end and you get a control room where structure is visible.
deeper_dives.why_it_matters: Solo operators running Founder-OS-style setups spend their day polling terminals. A spatial view that surfaces only blocked agents, and whose layout mirrors how work is partitioned, lets one person supervise ten times more agents without reading every log.
action_sketch: Emit one JSON event per agent state change (started, blocked, needs-review, done) from your harness hooks onto a local queue — Redis or a file tail is enough to start
Point Bot Crossing (or a 200-line Three.js scene) at that queue so blocked agents visibly raise hands; cluster agents by the repo/module they own to make the Conway structure visible
Run a week with dashboard versus without and log minutes-to-unblock per blocked agent
Falsifier: if minutes-to-unblock does not drop by at least a third versus a plain notification, the game layer is decoration and a notch widget wins
prerequisites: Willingness to treat this as an art-tech experiment first

deeper_dives.title: Selling to Agents — metered data for buyers that don't have eyes
deeper_dives.thesis: Three saves describe one gap. Quality publishers block AI crawlers, so AI search cites whatever is left. AI assistants favor the sponsored option in 18 of 23 models, so they are steerable buyers. Software is going headless, so agents pick tools by speed, cost and accuracy instead of interface. x402 revives HTTP 402 so an agent can pay a stablecoin micropayment per request. A one-person owner of a clean niche dataset can sit exactly in that gap — machine-legible, crawler-reachable, and metered.
deeper_dives.why_it_matters: This is distribution without an audience. The buyer is an agent that never sees your landing page, so a solo builder with good data competes on structure and price, not on ads. DejaViewed's own catalog and API are the obvious first item to sell.
action_sketch: Expose one niche dataset you own (start with the DejaViewed catalog's api/ JSON) as a free llms.txt summary plus a richer x402-metered endpoint with structured, citation-ready records.
Wrap the same endpoint as an MCP server and list it publicly so Claude and other agents can find it; log every request, free and paid, with user agent.
Run a 60-day A/B on price per call (free, 0.1c, 1c) and track how often your records show up in Perplexity and ChatGPT answers.
falsifier: if after 60 days you see plenty of free crawls but close to zero paid calls, agents are not buying yet. The demand side doesn't exist and this is a 2027 idea, not a 2026 one.
prerequisites: A dataset that is genuinely yours to sell

deeper_dives.why_it_matters: You can track the one variable the neocloud debt depends on with public price pages and a scheduled agent. Physical infrastructure with real order books, like chillers, is a different bet from GPU-hour rental, and this lens separates them.

Pull neocloud debt and contract maturities from public filings and plot rental price against the period when large contracts roll off.
Write a monthly one-page note: is GPU-hour price falling faster than token volume is rising? Paper only, no positions.
falsifier: if GPU-hour rental prices hold flat or rise while token prices fall, usage growth (Jevons) is absorbing the deflation and the tail-risk thesis is wrong.
prerequisites: A scheduled agent and a spreadsheet

deeper_dives.title: Who's Across the Table — forensics for the system trading against you
deeper_dives.thesis: Across the catalog, the systems you interact with are quietly optimizing against you: a puzzle game runs an on-device XGBoost model to time difficulty to your ad value, overnight and intraday returns run as a decades-long sawtooth, a bedroom spoofer tripped depth-reading algorithms in the 2010 Flash Crash, wash trading inflates crypto volume, and exchanges sold speed to HFTs. Agent-plus-Ghidra decompilation and cheap tick data mean one person can now audit the counterparty instead of guessing about it.
deeper_dives.why_it_matters: This is game theory made practical: before you look for edge, measure the edge that's already being taken from you — your fills, the hours you hold, the apps you pay. It's defensive leverage, and it often turns into an offensive idea, like simply holding overnight.
action_sketch: Split two years of SPY and QQQ returns into close-to-open and open-to-close legs, then subtract realistic open-gap spreads to see whether the overnight leg survives costs.
Export your own broker fills and compare each to the NBBO at the time, so you measure the price improvement or slippage you actually got.
For one paid or free-to-play app you use, run REA MCP on your own install and list every model or rule that adapts to you (authorized analysis only).
falsifier: if the overnight leg disappears after costs and your fills match or beat the NBBO, the counterparty isn't taking much from you at your size — move your effort to the strategy-loop dive.

deeper_dives.title: Mocap as Reward — teaching cheap robots to move like you
deeper_dives.thesis: The Microduck RL demo shows the classic failure: a loose reward function makes the robot 'stand' in a way nobody intended. The catalog also holds the fix, scattered across collections. FreeMoCap turns a webcam into markerless motion capture, HY-Motion produces motion from text on robot skeletons, and Blender plus a GPU contact solver can rehearse physical contact. Use captured or generated motion as an imitation reward on a cheap open robot. The reward-design trial and error becomes 'show it what you mean'.
deeper_dives.why_it_matters: Hobby robotics is gated by reward engineering more than by hardware. A webcam reference clip gives an individual the motion-prior pipeline that only labs used to have, for small expressive robots, animatronics and installations.
action_sketch: Reproduce the Microduck standing run in its sim with 4,096 envs; confirm the reward hack.
Record a 10-second webcam clip of a 'bob and look around' motion with FreeMoCap (or generate one with HY-Motion), retarget to Microduck's joints, and add a pose-tracking imitation term to the reward.
Compare policies: reward-only vs reward + imitation, scored by a blind viewer on 'looks intentional' and by joint-tracking error; deploy the winner to hardware if you have it.

Falsifier: if retargeting human motion to a duck-scale robot body produces infeasible joint targets that the policy can't track better than the plain reward, the motion prior is the wrong shape for small robots.
